sentence_stem: Had the committee been informed earlier,
correct_completion: the project would have been approved last year.
full_sentence: Had the committee been informed earlier, the project would have been approved last year.
acceptable_variants: the project would have been approved sooner.
the project might have been approved last year.

options.text: the project was approved last year.
options.why_wrong: The stem sets up a hypothetical condition, so the result needs 'would have + past participle'. A simple past states a fact instead.
'So' signals a result of something already known, not the hypothetical outcome that the inverted conditional requires.

options.text: the project would have been approved last year.
the project has been approved already.
options.why_wrong: The present perfect describes a completed situation without the hypothetical link that the stem demands.

explanation: The inverted form 'Had + subject + past participle' replaces 'If ... had been informed', so the main clause must use 'would have + past participle' to express an unreal past result.
translation: Si el comité hubiera sido informado antes, el proyecto habría sido aprobado el año pasado.
